source: A prediction registered BEFORE the event, so the result cannot be rationalised afterwards. Predicts the next Promitor/Beanironia alignment and states the protocol that turns observing it into a phase correction.

pair.note: Chosen well: fast relative motion makes the crossing sharp, and VH-331c's own accumulated error is small, so nearly the whole correction lands on VH-331a — the single worst-constrained body in the set at 24 deg.

prediction.FINAL: 2026-08-16T21:34Z — exact game elements, no observational correction of any kind
prediction.uncorrected: 2026-08-16T20:56Z +- 3.1 h, straight from the shipped rounded asset
prediction.corrected: 2026-08-16T21:50Z +- 1.4 h, rounded asset plus an observational correction (superseded)
prediction.watchWindow: 2026-08-16T20:25Z to 23:15Z, unchanged and still comfortably containing the final value
prediction.convergence: The exact-element answer and the observationally-corrected one agree to 16 minutes by wholly independent routes — one fitted from map angles, one derived from game data with no observation involved. That agreement is the check that matters here.
prediction.correctionMethod: SUPERSEDED. The original three-system capture was re-dated using ZV-759c/d — the lowest-error pair available, both slow bodies, 0.5 deg of accumulated phase between them — giving T1 = 15:18Z +- 0.9 h against the nine-angle fit's 15:04Z. VH-331 a/c read -27.4 deg there against a model -23.2 deg, so the pair carries a -4.2 deg correction, worth +0.9 h on the crossing.
prediction.errorBar: Deliberately not quoted in minutes. With VH-331's elements exact the model's own phase error for this pair is negligible, so what remains is the epoch constant and the gravitational constant the engine uses — neither boundable from data in hand, and both measured by the observation itself. A 51-minute bracket was quoted earlier in this campaign and was wrong; the lesson taken is to state the point estimate and let the observation set the bar. Expect roughly an hour.

whatTheObservationNowMeasures: The target changed when the elements did. Timing this crossing no longer measures a per-pair phase correction — with exact elements there is nothing left to correct — it measures the GLOBAL clock: the epoch, convolved with the engine's G. At 4.6 deg/h a crossing timed to +-5 min pins that combination to +-5 min against a 4,720-day baseline. Separating epoch from G needs a second conjunction in a system with a different revolution count, because G enters through the revolution count and the epoch does not.

predictedGapDegExact.comment: Promitor relative to Beanironia from exact elements; negative = behind and closing

predictedGapDeg.comment: SUPERSEDED — from the rounded asset plus the observational correction, kept for comparison

protocol.doNot: Do not try to eyeball the moment of alignment. The pair sits within a 4 deg reading error of aligned for about 1.7 h, so 'it looks lined up now' carries roughly the uncertainty the prediction already has and adds nothing.
protocol.do: Take two or three timestamped captures spaced about an hour apart across the window, noting the clock to the minute. Each yields a gap; the crossing follows by interpolation and needs no capture near the crossing itself.
protocol.why: At 4.6 deg/h a crossing timed to +-15 min pins the VH-331 a/c relative phase to +-1.15 deg, against the 24 deg the model carries today — roughly a twentyfold improvement, and it transfers almost entirely onto VH-331a.
protocol.generalisation: Conjunctions are the natural calibration event for this model: the observable is a sign change rather than an angle, and the quantity moves fastest exactly where it is being measured.

falsifiability: An observed crossing outside 20:25Z-23:15Z breaks the correction chain rather than the epoch — most likely the ZV-759c/d dating of the original capture, which rests on two bodies and a 0.9 h sigma. Outside about +-5 h it would instead indict the VH-331 identifications, which came from radius ratios and one confirmed pair.
